overview.description: Racing card game for 2–6 players. Each hand is a race to 1000 km (or 700 km in 2–3 player with optional extension). Players play distance cards to advance; opponents play hazards (Accident, Out of Gas, Flat Tire, Stop, Speed Limit) which are countered by remedies and prevented by safeties. First to reach the target distance wins the hand. Game ends when one side reaches 5000 cumulative points.

history.origins: Created in 1954 by Edmond Dujardin in France as 1000 Bornes; derived from the American game Touring (1906, William Janson Roche). Name refers to the approximate length of Route Nationale 7 from Paris to the Italian border. Parker Brothers licensed and published it in the US from 1962; at one point it outsold Monopoly.
timeline: 1954: Dujardin creates 1000 Bornes in Arcachon, France.
1960: Revised edition with updated artwork; bilingual cards.
1982: Parker Brothers revision with simplified card art.
Present: Published by Asmodee (US), Winning Moves, others; 26 known publishers worldwide.
history.evolution: Coup-fourré (playing a safety in response to the corresponding hazard for a 300-point bonus) was added compared to Touring. Spanish version Mil Hitos was popular in 1970s Spain; Dutch predecessor Stap op (1939) used cycling theme with same mechanics.
history.cultural: Listed in GAMES Magazine Hall of Fame. Advertised as a favorite of bridge champions; often played in teams of two (4 or 6 players).

setup.players: 2, 3, 4, or 6 players. Four or six players form teams of two sharing a tableau.
setup.deck: Dedicated Mille Bornes deck of 106 cards: 18 hazards, 38 remedies, 4 safeties, 46 distance cards (25, 50, 75, 100, 200 km).
setup.dealing: Shuffle and deal six cards to each player. Remainder forms the draw pile; a discard pile forms next to it. Each turn: draw one card from stock, then play one card to tableau or discard one. Hand size stays at six after play.

rules.objective: Win a hand by being first to play enough distance cards to reach the target (1000 km in 4- or 6-player team play; 700 km in 2- or 3-player with option to extend to 1000). Win the game by being first to reach 5000 cumulative points.
rules.gameplay: On your turn draw one card, then play one card or discard. Play Roll to drive; play distance cards (25–200 km) when Roll is showing; max two 200 km per hand. Play hazards on opponents; play remedies on your battle/speed area; play safeties for immunity and optional coup-fourré. Discard when no legal play. Hand ends when someone reaches target distance or all cards are played.
keyRules: Roll (Go) must show in your battle area before you can play distance cards; Right of Way safety waives this.
Speed Limit limits you to 25 and 50 km distance until End of Limit is played.
Each hazard has one remedy and one safety; safeties prevent that hazard for the rest of the hand.
Coup-fourré: play the matching safety when an opponent plays the hazard against you; hazard is removed and you score 300 bonus.
No more than two 200 km cards per player per hand; total distance cannot exceed target.

strategy.basic: Play distance when you can; save remedies for when you are hit; use hazards to slow the leader.
strategy.intermediate: Time hazards (Stop, Speed Limit) when the opponent has just played Roll; hold one safety for coup-fourré if you can afford the hand space.
strategy.advanced: In teams, coordinate so one partner holds safeties for coup-fourré while the other pushes distance; in 2–3 player consider calling Extension only when you can reach 1000 before opponents.
tips: Playing a safety gives an extra draw and another play; chain safeties when you have several.
Speed Limit limits the opponent to 25 and 50 km only until they play End of Limit.
Shutout (500 pts) requires completing the trip before the opponent has played any distance card.

list.name: Extension (2–3 player)
list.description: In 2- or 3-player play the target is 700 km. The first player to reach 700 km may either claim victory and end the hand, or call for an Extension that raises the target to 1000 km. First to 1000 km then wins the hand and scores a 200-point Extension bonus.
list.emptyOverridesReason: Extension only changes target distance (700 vs 1000 km); no engine constant overrides documented in sources.

play_card.description: Play one card to your tableau (Roll, distance, remedy, or safety) or play a hazard onto an opponent's tableau. Roll or remedy to own battle/speed area; distance to distance area when Roll is showing and within speed limit; safety to safety area; hazard to opponent's battle or speed area if allowed.
play_card.constraints: Legal only if the card type and current tableau state allow it (e.g. distance only when Roll is showing; hazard only on opponent who has Roll or empty speed area for Speed Limit).

draw.description: Draw one card from the stock at the start of your turn. Keeps hand at six cards after you play or discard.
draw.constraints: Once per turn at start of turn; from stock only.

discard.description: Discard one card from hand to the discard pile. Required when you have no legal play; otherwise optional. Discarded cards are out of play for the hand.
discard.constraints: One card per turn when chosen; must discard if no other legal action.

edgeCases.text: When an opponent plays a hazard against you, you may immediately play the matching safety (even out of turn); hazard is removed to discard, you score 300 bonus and draw a card, then take your normal turn.
Max two 200 km distance cards per player per hand.
Total distance played cannot exceed the target (1000 or 700 km); playing a distance card that would exceed target is illegal.
In 2–3 player, first to 700 km may call Extension to raise target to 1000 km; first to 1000 then wins the hand and gets Extension bonus.
Delayed action: 300 bonus for completing the trip after the draw pile is exhausted.
Safe trip: 300 bonus for completing without playing any 200 km cards. Shutout: 500 bonus if opponent played no distance cards.
Right of Way safety remedies both Stop and Speed Limit; with it you need not play Roll after remedying other hazards.
Multiple hazards may be stacked on one opponent; only the top hazard must be remedied (and Roll played if needed) before that player can play distance again.

engine.deckDescription: Mille Bornes uses a dedicated 106-card proprietary deck, not a standard 52-card pack. The deck has four card types: Hazards (18: Accident, Out of Gas, Flat Tire, Stop, Speed Limit), Remedies (38: Repairs, Gasoline, Spare Tire, Go/Roll, End of Speed Limit), Safeties (4: Driving Ace, Extra Tank, Puncture Proof, Right of Way), and Distance (46: 25, 50, 75, 100, 200 km cards). For schema compatibility this game references the Standard 52 triple; implementers should use the Mille Bornes deck composition.
engine.suitDescription: Mille Bornes has no traditional suits. Card types function as four categories: hazard (Accident, Out of Gas, Flat Tire, Stop, Speed Limit), remedy (matching counter for each hazard plus Roll and End of Limit), safety (Driving Ace, Extra Tank, Puncture Proof, Right of Way), and distance (25, 50, 75, 100, 200 km). Each safety pairs with one or two hazards and prevents or counters them.
engine.rankDescription: Distance cards have values 25, 50, 75, 100, and 200 km; at most two 200 km cards may be played per player per hand. Hazards, remedies, and safeties have no numeric rank; they are matched by type (e.g. Flat Tire pairs with Spare Tire remedy and Puncture Proof safety). Roll and End of Limit are remedies for Stop and Speed Limit respectively.

synthesis.shortDescription: Racing card game. Drive 1000 km by playing distance cards; fend off hazards with remedies and safeties. First to 5000 points wins.

prompts.human: Mille Bornes: draw one, play one or discard. Play Roll to drive, distance to advance, hazards on opponents, remedies and safeties on yourself. First to 1000 km wins the hand; first to 5000 points wins the game.
prompts.ai: Game: Mille Bornes. Logic: draw one per turn from stock; play one card (Roll, distance, remedy, safety, or hazard on opponent) or discard. Hand ends at target distance or when all cards played. Score by distance, safeties, coup-fourré, trip completion, and bonuses; game to 5000.

scoring.description: Points per hand: 1 per km traveled; 100 per safety; 300 bonus for all four safeties; 300 per coup-fourré; 400 for completing the trip; 300 delayed action (trip after stock exhausted); 300 safe trip (no 200 km cards); 200 extension bonus; 500 shutout (opponent played no distance). Game ends when one side reaches 5000 points; if both exceed 5000 in the same hand, higher total wins.
scoring.winCondition: First to reach 5000 cumulative points. Each hand won by first to reach target distance (1000 km or 700 km in 2–3 player with optional extension).

nullReasons.cardValues: Scoring uses distance (1 per km), safety and trip bonuses, not per-card point values.
